channel.title: GeoAI Research Radar — Personal Literature Feed
channel.description: New papers on wildfire smoke, mobility, environmental justice and GeoAI, curated from OpenAlex.

item.title: Residency duration, risk perceptions, and recent PM2.5 exposure predict protective behaviors toward wildfire smoke: A comparison of recent migrants and long-term Idaho residents
item.description: Air Quality, Atmosphere & Health — Compares perceived wildfire-smoke risk and protective behavior among recent migrants and long-term Idaho residents.

item.title: An integrated framework for resilient urban mobility: coupling disruption taxonomy, equilibrium modelling and participatory validation
item.description: Journal of Infrastructure Preservation and Resilience — Introduces a framework for urban transport resilience using disruption taxonomy, equilibrium modelling and participatory validation.

item.title: Spatio-temporal trends in wildfire smoke exposures at schools and childcare centers in the United States and implications for child and adolescent health
item.description: Environmental Research — Examines spatiotemporal patterns of wildfire smoke exposure at schools and childcare facilities and their implications for children and adolescents.

item.title: Beyond connectivity: Travel behavior and hidden inequities in human mobility resilience
item.description: Transportation Research Part D: Transport and Environment — Proposes a behaviorally grounded perspective on mobility resilience, examining travel constraints and inequality under transportation disruption.

item.title: Fired up for work: Examining the relationship between environmentally-vulnerable work and population health outcomes in the context of wildfire smoke exposures
item.description: Population and Environment — Examines how environmentally vulnerable work intersects with wildfire smoke exposure and population health.

item.title: A multimodal transformer neural network framework for fine-scale wildfire occurrence forecasting
item.description: Engineering with Computers — Develops a multimodal transformer-based framework for fine-scale wildfire occurrence forecasting.

item.title: Urban mobility responses to wildfire smoke-related air quality advisories in Montréal, Canada
item.description: Health & Place — Uses bike-share, metro, bus and running data to examine mobility responses to wildfire smoke air-quality advisories, including spatial variation across Montréal.

item.title: Wildfire impact potential along routes shapes mobility patterns during the evacuation period
item.description: International Journal of Disaster Risk Reduction — Studies how wildfire impact potential along evacuation routes relates to observed mobility patterns, comparing route-level and destination-level measures.

item.title: Wildland Fires in the US between 2007 and 2018: Characterizing Equity in Exposures and Health Impacts
item.description: Environmental Science & Technology — Analyzes inequalities in wildfire exposure and related health burdens across population groups in the United States.

item.title: From Outdoor to Indoor: Amplified Inequities in Wildfire PM2.5 Exposure across the Contiguous United States
item.description: Environmental Science & Technology — Studies inequalities in wildfire-related fine particulate exposure when considering the difference between outdoor and indoor environments.

item.title: Smoke signals: Understanding temporal dynamics of wildfire exposure on health and education
item.description: Journal of Environmental Economics and Management — Examines wildfire smoke exposure in Chile across multiple seasons and studies temporal relationships with health and educational outcomes.

item.title: Behavioral responses to wildfire smoke: Insights from smartphone location data
item.description: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences — Uses smartphone location data to examine behavioral responses to wildfire smoke and how responses differ across education groups.

item.title: Exploring the spatial association between wildfire risk and social vulnerability in the continental US
item.description: International Journal of Wildland Fire — Applies bivariate local indicators of spatial association to identify where wildfire risk and social vulnerability overlap across US census tracts.

item.title: A Multi-Source Reconstruction of the 2024 Jasper Wildfire Complex Evacuation and Reentry Periods
item.description: Transportation Research Interdisciplinary Perspectives — Combines mobility data, traffic counts and social media to reconstruct wildfire evacuation, reentry timing and transportation constraints in Jasper, Canada.

item.title: Evaluation of Smoke Exposure Risk from January 2025 Los Angeles Wildfires Using Crowdsourced Data
item.description: ACS ES&T Air — Analyzes indoor and outdoor PM2.5 from PurpleAir sensors during the January 2025 Los Angeles fires, examining exposure differences across communities.

item.title: Measuring evacuation rates from mobility data during the McDougall Creek wildfire in British Columbia, Canada
item.description: Computers, Environment and Urban Systems — Estimates neighborhood-scale wildfire evacuation rates from network mobility data and examines spatial patterns and correlates of evacuation behavior.

item.title: Increasing Exposures to Compound Wildfire Smoke and Extreme Heat Hazards in California, 2011–2020
item.description: Earth's Future — Characterizes compound wildfire-smoke and extreme-heat exposure in California and evaluates spatial distributions of population vulnerability.

item.title: The impact of wildfire smoke on traffic evacuation dynamics
item.description: Safety Science — Uses a virtual-reality driving simulator to assess how wildfire smoke visibility affects vehicle speeds and evacuation traffic dynamics.

item.title: Unveiling the Dynamics of Human Mobility in Response to Wildfire-Induced Air Quality Degradation: An Examination of the 2019 Kincade Fire
item.description: Journal of Management in Engineering — Investigates how wildfire-related deterioration of PM2.5 air quality relates to population mobility, including differences across vulnerable communities.

item.title: On the Opportunities and Challenges of Foundation Models for GeoAI (Vision Paper)
item.description: ACM Transactions on Spatial Algorithms and Systems — A vision paper examining how foundation models can be developed and evaluated across geospatial tasks, including remote sensing, health and urban geography.
